At each gathering members would discuss a short story, a short work of non-fiction and perhaps a poem, all of which he would choose and provide via email. The purpose is both literary and social: to enjoy one another’s company by sharing thoughts and feelings about the art of writing. The group was there to discuss Born a Crime by South African comedian Trevor Noah. It was published in 2016, favorably received, and became a No. 1 New York Times Bestseller. It was also named one of the best books of the year by the Times. The book tells of Noah growing up in his native South Africa during the apartheid era. He is the mixed-race son of a white Swiss-German father and a black mother. Noah was classified as a “coloured” in accordance with the country’s apartheid system of racial classification at that time. He writes that under apartheid it was hard for him to fit into this racist society because it was a crime “for to be born as a mixedrace baby.” Born a Crime tells Noah’s stories, but also pays homage to his mother who grew up in a hut with fourteen occupants. She is stubborn, fearless, and a fiercely religious woman who took her son to three churches every Sunday, a prayer meeting on Tuesday, Bible study on Wednesday, and youth church on Thursday. This is happening when black South Africans were rioting in the streets, and most people were staying inside the safety of their homes. Despite growing up in poverty in a racist society and having a part-time biological father and later an abusive stepfather, Noah navigates through this world. He uses his intelligence, social and mental agility, as well as his fluency in languages and ability to mimic others, to be accepted as a mixed race child and become an amazing performer. His mother provides tough love and “oldschool, Old Testament discipline” as he goes. This was one of those unique books where all the readers enjoyed it with little to criticize. Some readers didn’t know much about Noah except that he is a comic. The “stories from a South African childhood” were revelatory about Noah and life then in South Africa. Noah is able to deal with a dark time in a light tone. He is cleaver and humorous, but the book is not funny. He doesn’t preach, so everyone including readers just looking to be entertained find the book acceptable. Those members of the group who listened to the book’s audio version found it especially enjoyable. Noah is a gifted performer and mimic. His reading made the different situations and people with different styles of speech all the more fun. Some readers questioned how factually accurate the different stories were, but it was accepted they might be “family stories” where precise accuracy is not that important. The group previously selected The Killer Angels by Michael Shaara for May, The Hare with Amber Eyes by Edmund de Waal for June, and How Beautiful We Were by Cameroonian-American novelist Imbolo Mbue for July. articles.text: On Sunday morning, April 2, a resident interrupted catalytic converter thieves as they tried to steal the emission device from his Toyota parked on Florada Avenue. The resident woke up at 6:30 a.m. after hearing sawing noises and approached the suspects who were in a silver Kia sedan with the engine running. After being spotted, one suspect pointed a black Glock handgun at the resident. He said something in Spanish to the resident, who put his hands up and retreated to his home. No shots were fired, and there were no injuries. The suspects then fled on Florada towards La Salle. Catalytic converters are coveted for the precious metals within and nationwide crime rings facilitate the extraction and sale of the metals. The resident’s converter was damaged, but not removed. The Police Department strongly urge residents not to interfere with crimes in progress. “For your own safety, when you witness a crime, please call 9-1-1 immediately and stay on the phone with dispatchers until officers arrive. The best way to help our officers protect you is to stay inside your home and provide the dispatcher with a thorough description of the suspects and the vehicle associated with them,” the police stated. A crime in progress requires a 9-1-1 call. The non-emergency dispatch line for the Piedmont Police is 420-3000.

articles.text: The Wisdom of Solomon is one of the books of the Apocrypha. Also called the Deuterocanonicals, these are books found in the Catholic Bible but not in the Protestant Bible or the Hebrew Scriptures. The Wisdom of Solomon was written in the late first century BCE or early first century CE meaning it comes from the time, or very nearly from the time, of Jesus. articles.text: Gonzales said that, since then, Public Works has held “at least three public meetings, and then a number of follow up meetings with individuals who are impacted by the project, both one on one and then in small neighborhood working groups.” The meetings focused on traffic impact, pedestrian counts, maintaining access to driveways, and maintaining adequate sight distance for drivers turning left onto Nova from Magnolia. Gonzales said that the new plan was “generally … very well received.” Jane Lim and Mary Wells, two residents who live by the intersection of Magnolia and Nova and who spoke at the meeting, echoed Gonzales’ statement. Although minor changes could have been made, they said — Lim emphasized more traffic-calming measures for speeding vehicles and Wells emphasized drought-tolerant planting on the island — they both commended the city for arriving at a plan which addressed major resident concerns.
